Most apps encourage you to leave a rating, and as such they also encourage you to leave five stars, but seeing as this app does that before even letting you try it, I feel that this is completely disingenuous and unethical. title: Why Not Offer a Free Version? Keep the App Experience Clean
body: Hey, cool idea, but I wanted to share some feedback from a developer’s perspective. I don’t understand why the app forces users into a subscription right from the start. While I get that you might rely on premium services (like AI integrations or Plaid), why not adopt a freemium model? It would be great to allow users to explore the app first, even in a limited capacity, to see if it meets their needs before committing to a subscription. For example, you could offer a demo mode to showcase features, like what the Copilot financial app does. Alternatively, you could allow access to basic features to encourage users to explore and feel confident about subscribing. Even offering a 1-2 month free trial could help users experience the app’s benefits without feeling locked out from the start. Overall, I think it’s a good concept, and I appreciate the innovation. However, the onboarding experience feels a bit restrictive with the current paywall. Giving users a chance to see the app in action before subscribing could go a long way in building trust and improving user experience. Best of luck with the app, and I hope you continue growing and expanding to other countries! Thanks for your hard work!

I genuinely do not understand how this is useful at all. Not to mention, it takes like a week to process one credit card payment. AND on top of this, you can't make any payments if you don't have $100 in your checking account. So basically if you have $99 in your checking, you aren't allowed to make a $20 credit card payment. It was way faster to just make credit card payments myself. In a month, I paid off $90 using ditch, and $600 by simply logging into my bank account and paying it myself. Don't bother with this app.
